title: POC Hypercare Onboarding Checklist and Labs Schedule
summary: Working doc for managing the immediate hypercare phase after POC kickoff. Focus: shorten time-to-first-success, structured lab sessions for customer engineers, and clear ownership for rollback/fallbacks.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture an actionable onboarding checklist and day-by-day lab schedule to get customer dev + infra teams to a deterministic demo/validation state within 10 working days.
- This is intentionally pragmatic: a mix of synchronous labs and asynchronous setup tasks, with explicit fallbacks and 'fast fail' gates.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: fintech startup, regulated data; on-prem private deployment evaluated.
- Goal: prove inference latency < 80ms P95 for 256-token prompts under 5 RPS and embedding throughput of 200 qps for batch embed jobs.
- Timebox: 2-week POC window, first week focused on integration + smoke, second week on accuracy/regression checks and performance tuning.
- Resources: 1 solutions engineer (Aisha), 1 infra lead (Miguel), 2 customer engineers (CE-Lead + CE-Dev).

Prework (before Day 0):
- Customer to provide network connectivity diagram and IP allowlist.
- Customer to create a service account and share KMS test key (or provide details for HSM integration notes).
- SE to prepare a compact model bundle (quantized) and a reference prompt set (50 queries).
- Setup a shared Slack channel and one PagerDuty escalation for the POC window.

Day-by-day labs schedule (high level):
- Day 0 (Kickoff call): align success criteria, confirm roles, run through emergency rollback plan. Quick demo of the sample app.
- Day 1 (Network + Access lab): validate IPs, test certificate handshake, confirm KMS integration; SE does live walkthrough of container startup logs and CLI.
- Day 2 (Model ingestion + routing lab): push model bundle, verify model catalog entry, exercise routing policy to fallback model variant.
- Day 3 (Inference smoke + latency baseline): run 100 sample requests, capture P50/P95, check KV-cache behavior for repeated prefixes.
- Day 4 (Batch embedding run): run embedding job on 10k rows; inspect throughput, memory footprint; iterate on batch size settings.
- Day 5 (Canary & trace day): execute canary rollout with 5% traffic, collect traces and token-level cost breakdown.
- Day 6 (Offline tuning day): SE tunes batching and quantization profile; infra lead validates GPU metrics under load.
- Day 7 (Customer self-run lab): customer engineers perform scripted integration and produce runbook notes.
- Day 8 (Regression checks): run prompt set, run quality checks vs baseline; collect failure cases for follow-up.
- Day 9 (Final demo prep): consolidate dashboards, prepare slides and short recording of flows.
- Day 10 (Final demo & handoff): demo to stakeholders, capture decision (go/no-go), list next steps for Dedicated or Private procurement.

Task tracker (as checklist, mark status during daily standups):
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled and calendar invites sent
- [ ] Network allowlist verified
- [ ] Service account + KMS access validated
- [ ] Model bundle uploaded and sanity-tested
- [ ] Latency smoke run completed (baseline metrics saved)
- [ ] Embedding full-run completed and logs archived
- [ ] Canary rollout executed and traces saved
- [ ] Runbook draft created by customer engineers
- [ ] Final demo recording created
- [ ] Post-POC evaluation meeting scheduled

Fast failures & fallbacks (explicit):
- If model upload fails repeatedly: fall back to 'hosted-sample' model and validate the orchestration behavior.
- If KMS/HSM not available within 48 hours: pivot to test KMS tokens (ephemeral) and mark as compliance risk in the final report.
- If latency targets not met on private infra: propose a Dedicated pilot with same config and compare perf numbers (automate side-by-side run).

Acceptance criteria (short list):
- Measurable: P95 latency < 80ms for target sample under the stated RPS OR clearly documented perf delta with proposed mitigations.
- Functional: customer app can make authenticated requests and receive streaming responses in expected format.
- Operational: runbook with steps to restart services, rotate keys, and roll back model versions exists and is validated by the customer engineers.
- Security: minimal audit logs enabled and an acceptance note from security reviewer (could be an email).

Metrics to capture (for wrap-up doc):
- Latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, GPU utilization, memory headroom, embedding qps, average token cost estimate.
- Number of retries / 5xx errors during each lab.
- Time-to-first-success (TFS): time from kickoff to first successful authenticated inference returned to the customer app.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Network complexity (multi-VPC peering): schedule pre-lab with customer network team; reserve extra day for troubleshooting.
- Nonstandard KMS/HSM: have a fallback config with ephemeral test keys and highlight as compliance discussion item.
- Customer-side CI gating: ask customer to allocate one engineer full-time during Days 1-3.

Notes to self and TODOs (informal):
- Bring a small script to scrape token-level cost from the trace export (Miguel will help finalize).
- Prepare two short troubleshooting playbooks: `restart-agent` and `reindex-model-cache`. Keep them < 10 steps.
- Remind CE-Lead to export sample errors and share the top 5 failure traces before Day 8.
- Consider a short 20-min office-hours on Day 6 for informal Q&A. Put placeholder in calendar.

Post-POC handoff checklist:
- Final metrics snapshot uploaded to Confluence
- Runbook accepted and signed off by CE-Lead
- Decision recorded (next: Dedicated trial / Private deployment / Stop)
- If go: create procurement ticket and initial Dedicated capacity estimate.

Unresolved questions (to capture in final report):
- Does customer need SIEM integration for audit logs or is S3 export sufficient?
- Are there any regulatory constraints on model weights leaving the premises? Need legal sign-off.

Appendix: quick command snippets (for labs)
- Model push: `rwdctl model push --bundle model.tar.gz --name poc-test-v1`
- Start agent: `rwdctl agent start --config poc-minimal.yaml`
- Simple latency probe: `ab -n 100 -c 2 http://localhost:8080/v1/infer`

This doc is a working artifact — update checklist statuses daily and paste short standup notes under the top section. Keep final version tidy before sending to customer as a readout.
